The in-process trigger can be swapped for a plugin or cloud-managed scheduler.
Due scheduled tasks are queued and the highest-priority pending task runs next.
The model can create, list, edit, pause, resume, run and remove jobs from conversation.
The agent schedules a future point when the same session resumes with a prompt (after N seconds, at a time, or on cron), and can list or cancel its wakeups.
/loop [interval] <prompt> re-wakes the current conversation on a fixed or self-paced cadence until done, a count, or a judge says stop.
A recurring job proposes its own next check time, clamped to min/max bounds.
A periodic check-in (default 30 min) reads a HEARTBEAT checklist and runs only when there is something to do, with an interval setting.
Active hours, quiet windows and fire gates
Proactive work respects active hours, quiet hours, weekends, days off and travel through pluggable shouldFire gates.
The owner pauses all scheduled and proactive work for a period with one switch.
After a check runs, a small model (or a [SILENT] reply) decides whether the result is worth messaging the user about.
A cheap probe (script or URL) runs each tick and the model only wakes when its output changes, so watches stay silent when nothing changed.
A script runs before (or instead of) the model and decides whether to fire, passing state and a message; a script that wants approval asks first.
Each job keeps a small key-value scratch (cursors, watermarks, checklist) between runs.
A job can run a shell command or a headless script with the agent's tools on schedule, with no model call.
Trigger and payload scripts can call configured MCP servers as functions, scoped by the job's allowed servers.
A job runs in the main session, the conversation that created it, a fresh isolated session or a named one, and its turns stay in a conversation of their own.
A conversation header links to the scheduled tasks bound to it.
Expired per-run sessions are pruned on a retention schedule while live descendants are kept.
Each job pins its own provider, model and reasoning effort, falling back to the default.

A job stores its own tool policy and the creator's authority at creation, so unattended runs never widen what they can do.
Cron prompts and trigger payloads are scanned for injection and exfiltration patterns and framed as outside data.
Jobs whose prompt or script would restart or stop the gateway from inside it are refused.
Finished runs are delivered to the origin chat, a home channel, any platform:chat, a webhook or nowhere, with a dry-run preview of where each job will deliver.
Run results are queued in a restart-safe outbox that a delivery worker sends with retries, parking undeliverable sends for later.
A delivered cron result is seeded into the chat's session so the user can reply and continue with the job's context.
A job injects the latest output of upstream jobs into its prompt (collect, triage, ship).
A job attaches skills whose bodies load into its prompt at fire time.
A job runs its agent and scripts inside a chosen project folder.
Jobs can be created paused for review or a manual run before they start firing.
Declarative automations from files and git
Automations defined in files (markdown with frontmatter, declared keys) or a git repo are reconciled into the store, upserting only declared fields.
Automations export to a portable file and import back, including merging a foreign store.
Authenticated endpoints let outside services wake an agent or submit a turn; the door stays closed until the owner opens it, and routes can be managed at runtime.
Named webhook routes render message templates from the payload ({{field.path}}) and route or fan out to agents and sessions.
Normalized outside events (PR opened, Slack event, signed MCP event, webhook) start matching automations through a durable ingress with leases, backoff and dead-lettering.
A named trigger bound to a session can be fired from a local command or stdin and is delivered at least once.
Agent lifecycle and run-completion events are POSTed to URLs, HMAC-signed (Standard Webhooks style), with retries and a bounded queue.
Outbound automation webhook URLs are validated and private or loopback targets refused unless allowed.
A watched mailbox starts an isolated restricted session per new allowed email, gating senders by DKIM/SPF/DMARC; Gmail uses Pub/Sub push.
Agents subscribe to PR reviews, comments, CI and mentions and get them as signals or replies.
A watcher on a command's output, a stream or a WebSocket, or a command exiting, wakes the agent with the buffered events.
Long MCP submit/status/cancel tools become durable background tasks the agent can list or cancel, with notifications.
Submit a task to the background hub and exit; it runs there and notifies on completion (/bg).

Outputs from several matching hooks merge with defined precedence for decisions and context.
Hooks before and after model calls see a stable, versioned request/response format.
A hook asks a model (or a sub-agent) for an allow or block decision against written criteria.
A hook calls an MCP tool with arguments filled from the event fields.
Oversized hook context is saved to a temp file and replaced by a preview and path.
Converts Claude Code hook settings into this app's hook events.
Lists hooks with status and lets the user enable or disable each, from a panel, CLI or API.
Ready-made hooks (block rm -rf, desktop notify, typecheck on change, memory logger).
A user program runs with a JSON payload when a turn completes, for custom alerts.
Folder-based hook packages (HOOK.md/HOOK.yaml + handler) run on gateway, command and message lifecycle events and install from npm, archives or URLs.
On /new or /reset the ending session's context is saved to a dated memory file.
Runs the workspace BOOT.md instructions when the gateway starts.
Logs command events to a central audit file.
Posts a visible chat notice when compaction starts and finishes.
Injects extra workspace files into agent context on bootstrap.
Curated starter jobs are offered as one-tap accept or dismiss cards, and recommended automations show on home.
A gallery of pre-written automation templates (blueprints) that fill a form, a slash command or a chat seed.
Prebuilt automations ship setup manifests with a capability check, prerequisites review, required inputs and metrics.
Seeded routines like a morning brief, reminder digest and evening check-in, plus a daily brief of agent results, so the assistant messages you first when switched on.
Reminder fires escalate by priority (retry, cross-channel), snooze resets the ladder.
A fired task completes itself when the user acknowledges, replies or the subject changes.
Triggers relative to wake time, bedtime or a calendar event start.
The model picks reminder content and timing but delivery is pinned to the verified private chat.
Owner life surfaces (reminders, alarms, todos, routines)
Owner-facing actions for reminders, alarms, todos and routines over one shared engine.
A drafted message scheduled to send later is persisted whole so it survives restarts.
On iOS, background tasks wake the agent so scheduled work runs while the app is backgrounded.
UI events are watched and at most one scoped helpful offer is surfaced under governance rules.
With autonomy on, a background tick lets the agent think and act on its own.
Long-horizon goals (quarter, year, life) are first-class objects whose check-ins run on the scheduler and record responses.
A goal stays active across turns; a judge model decides after each turn whether it is met, with budgets and pause, resume and stop.
Goals carry explicit completion criteria and quality gates; /subgoal adds criteria mid-run.
Agent-managed todos, follow-ups, handoffs and reminders with status and priority, reviewable by the user.
Scheduled CI workflows run the agent to triage issues, find duplicates, implement TODOs, sweep issues or track upstream releases.
Backups run on a schedule to local, git, WebDAV, S3 or offsite targets.
One shared timer runs periodic maintenance (cleanup, re-indexing connected sources, skill review) in worker processes.
Run one prompt non-interactively from the CLI, a file or stdin with text, JSON or stream-JSON output and exit codes for scripts and CI.
Command stream into a running agent
An outside process sends NDJSON commands (start, message, cancel) over stdin or an input file to a long-lived agent.
A running session mirrors structured events to a side channel so other tools can follow along.
Other programs start, resume, cancel and message tasks and subscribe to task events through an SDK, extension API or IPC socket.

A recipe runs other recipes as subagent tasks.
Recipes encode into links that open in the desktop app.

ACP clients list, load, save and start sessions from recipes.
Desktop editor for recipes with sub-recipes, model and extension selectors and a schema editor.
Code-built workflows with typed steps and .then, .branch, .parallel, .foreach and loops, nested workflows and validated inputs, saved with steps that survive a restart.
A step suspends with a payload (for approval or input) and the run resumes later from where it stopped.
Re-run a past run from any step with changed input, replaying earlier step results.
Active runs recover after a crash, with state checkpointed after each step, or run on Inngest or Temporal.
Workflows execute through pubsub events so steps run on distributed workers with fencing and retries.

Steps read and write a typed workflow-level state object.

Step fields use templates over parameters, trigger payload and earlier outputs.

A step makes templated HTTP calls with authorization checks on each redirect.
Steps for free-form browser tasks, navigation goals, single actions and schema extraction.
Download and upload files, parse CSV/Excel/ZIP/PDF, fill and split PDFs, export records as Parquet.
A step sends templated email with attachments over SMTP.
A step reads messages from a connected Gmail or Outlook inbox.

A predefined step plan (JSON or workflow) executes step by step through the policy-checked executor, including batches of plans.

Rules bound to sources start agent sessions on work-item transitions and reconcile external issues on a schedule.

One view of scheduled and triggered automations with search, on/off switch, owner name, health badge and Run now.
A detail page with prompt, configuration and an activity log of runs with stdout/stderr, and recent runs in the sidebar.
Edit name, prompt, schedule, timeout, profile and plugins with validation before saving.
Success rate, durations, cost totals and per-run sparklines computed from run history.
